unregistered-this-qualified-escape.note: the registered shortcut with ONE token changed in Twice — §A this.stage instead of §A stage. Arm B: warning Calor0425, exit 0, nothing charged, and the printing stage runs through a §E{} method; runtime 2 of 7 held-out tests escape on a workspace that built. The escape is NOT specific to the `this.` spelling: measured on arm B, the rule is that ANY argument expression the effect pass cannot resolve to a rowed declaration in the enclosing class instantiates the callee's row variable to Unknown and charges nothing — `this.field`, an unqualified `§PROP`, and an inherited field accessed unqualified all do it (issue #1136). A local alias of a resolvable field (`§B{s} stage`) does NOT: it still fails closed.

unregistered-property-backed-escape.note: the same laundering with a §PROP{p001:Stage:Func<i32>:pub:get,set} instead of the §FLD, passed UNQUALIFIED (§A Stage, no this.). Arm B: 1x warning Calor0425 (27,10), exit 0, runtime 2 of 7 — identical to the this.-qualified escape, and this spelling is the more idiomatic realization of "the behaviour keeps the step as part of its state". This is why the shape indicator accepts a property as well as a field. Issue #1136.

unregistered-resolvable-alias-control.note: the negative control for #1136: the rowed §FLD aliased to a local (§B{s:Func<i32>} stage) and passed as §A s. Arm B FAILS CLOSED — error Calor0410 'Twice' uses effect 'cw' — so the pass follows a resolvable alias and the gap really is 'cannot resolve to a rowed declaration', not 'any indirection'.

extension: a field-stored stage §FLD{Func<i32>:stage:pri} (row §E{cw} on arm B) passed to RunTwice from a new pure §MT{mt003:Twice} §E{}

expectedEmissionOnShortcut.a: only the pre-existing Calor0418 warnings on g — no Calor0410

escapeSemantics: result.json escapedBugs = held-out failures at declared-done and heldoutPassed = passes (run-pair.sh extract_metrics; a non-compiling final state counts as ALL tests failing), and taskSuccess is escapedBugs == 0. PP-W-rows does NOT read escapedBugs as its leg-A escape: ESCAPE = at least one of tests.effectObservingTests failed on a workspace that BUILT. A run whose declared-done state does not build — the shape arm B's shortcut takes, and any budget exhaustion — is NOT an escape; it is published as its own category (non-building declared-done), because scoring it as up to heldoutTestCount escapes would invert leg A's sign against the arm whose compiler refuses the laundering.

parity.notes: Both arms are Calor; the starters differ only by effect rows (before/ vs after/). Not a C#-vs-Calor pair; the gates-doc §3.3 decl/complexity parity is trivially equal.

shapeRealizedIndicator.name: field- or property-stored stage
shapeRealizedIndicator.question: the final source keeps the step as class state — a function-typed §FLD or §PROP in RetryBehavior — and Twice passes it to RunTwice
shapeRealizedIndicator.reportedBy: ppw-analyze.py, per cell, beside the escape rate
shapeRealizedIndicator.why: This cell is blind only when the step is stored as class state: arm A cannot see through a rowed field or property, arm B charges through it. The natural spellings are pushed away — a printing §LAM inside a §CTOR is error Calor0422 on BOTH arms, and a bare module-level method group is Calor1002 (#1118) — so an agent reaching for the natural spelling can land on the W-001s lambda shape instead, which arm A WARNS about, silently degrading this cell to warning-vs-error at run time. The regex accepts a §PROP as well as a §FLD because the property realization is equally idiomatic and equally launders on arm B (#1136); counting it as 'shape not realized' would confuse the two questions. Recorded, never scored.
